definitions.explanation: Acting or speaking beyond one's position or authority; overstepping one's bounds. Used as a humble self-deprecation when speaking up in a situation where one might be considered unqualified.

examples.japanese: {僭越|せんえつ}⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、⟦{一言|ひとこと}→一言：03708_hitokoto⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧。
examples.english: If I may be so bold, I would like to say a few words.

examples.japanese: {僭越|せんえつ}で⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ございます→ございます：01300_gozaimasu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{乾杯|かんぱい}→乾杯：00176_kanpai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音頭|おんど}→音頭：09782_ondo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}らせて→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦いただきます→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧。
examples.english: Though it's presumptuous of me, I will lead the toast.

examples.japanese: {僭越|せんえつ}⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、ご⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{述|の}べさせて→述べる：02389_noberu⟧⟦いただきます→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧。
examples.english: If you'll permit me, I'd like to share my opinion.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used as a humble disclaimer ({僭越|せんえつ}⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧ or {僭越|せんえつ}で⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ございます→ございます：01300_gozaimasu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧) before speaking, especially in formal situations like ceremonies or meetings. The speaker acknowledges they may be overstepping by speaking up.
- Wedding speeches (when not the main host)
- Business meetings (junior person offering opinion)
- Formal ceremonies (leading toasts, speeches)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {僭越|せんえつ}⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧ - though it's presumptuous of me
- {僭越|せんえつ}で⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ございます→ございます：01300_gozaimasu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ - though I may be overstepping

ETYMOLOGY:
{僭|せん} (to overstep) + {越|えつ} (to exceed) - literally "exceeding one's bounds"
